description: Apply global polish: enhance Sidebar with icon shift animations and badge animations, ensure consistent EmptyState and Skeleton usage across all 21 screens, add micro-interactions to all buttons and inputs via CSS enhancements, verify mobile responsive polish, complete accessibility audit with prefers-reduced-motion and keyboard navigation testing.
steps: Read context.json and all previous FEAT findings

Sidebar Enhancement (src/v2/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx): Keep existing layoutId animation on active indicator and add subtle glow, add icon shift animation (translateX 2px on hover) to nav items, wrap badge counts with AnimatedBadge component that pulses when count changes, add hover glow ring to user avatar, enhance sign out button with hover scale transition, keep existing mobile drawer animation and verify backdrop blur works

Global Empty States Audit: Review all 21 view files, ensure every potential no-data scenario uses EmptyState component with appropriate Lucide icon, clear title, helpful description, optional CTA button, list files that need EmptyState additions in findings

Loading States Audit: Review all 21 view files, replace generic loading spinners with appropriate Skeleton components (SkeletonCard for card grids, SkeletonText for lists, Skeleton for individual elements), add custom chart skeletons matching chart dimensions, add table row skeletons, list files that need Skeleton additions in findings

Global CSS Micro-Interactions (src/index.css): Verify existing button/input transitions are smooth, add chevron/arrow icon rotation on hover (.group-hover:rotate-180 type patterns), ensure button active state has scale:0.98 feedback, add link underline slide-in animation, ensure badge pulse animation exists for updates, verify toast entrance/exit animations are smooth

Mobile Responsive Audit: Test all 21 screens at 375px width (iPhone SE) and 768px width (iPad), ensure all grids use responsive Tailwind classes (sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3), verify mobile drawer animation works smoothly, ensure modals go full-screen on mobile vs centered on desktop, verify touch targets are minimum 44x44px for all buttons, list any mobile issues found in findings

Accessibility Audit: Verify all animations respect prefers-reduced-motion (check useReducedMotion hook in all motion components), ensure all interactive elements have focus-visible styles (already in index.css), add aria-label to all icon-only buttons across all 21 views, verify heading hierarchy is correct (h1 → h2 → h3) on each screen, run manual color contrast check on at least 5 screens (should pass with current palette), test keyboard navigation with Tab key on 5 representative screens to ensure logical order, list any accessibility issues found in findings

Final verification: npm run dev, systematically test all 21 screens, verify Sidebar enhancements work, spot-check empty states, spot-check loading skeletons (throttle network in DevTools), verify mobile responsive at 375px, test with prefers-reduced-motion enabled, test keyboard navigation
Document findings: any remaining issues, any screens that need follow-up, summary of global enhancements applied
acceptance_criteria: Sidebar: Nav icons shift right 2px on hover, badge counts use AnimatedBadge and pulse on change, active indicator has subtle glow, user avatar has hover glow, sign out button scales on hover, mobile drawer works smoothly
Every screen with no-data scenarios has EmptyState component with appropriate icon and messaging
Every screen with loading states has appropriate Skeleton components replacing generic spinners
Global CSS has smooth micro-interactions on buttons, inputs, icons, links, badges
All 21 screens are mobile responsive and stack properly at 375px width
All modals adapt to full-screen on mobile
All screens have correct heading hierarchy
Keyboard navigation works logically on tested screens
verification: Test Sidebar: hover nav items to see icon shift, verify badge animation (change count by triggering action), hover avatar to see glow, test mobile drawer at 375px
Spot-check empty states: Visit 5-6 screens with no data (clear filters or use empty account), verify EmptyState component renders with proper icon, title, description
Spot-check loading states: Throttle network to Slow 3G in DevTools, navigate through 5-6 screens, observe skeleton screens appear before data loads
Mobile responsive test: Resize to 375px, visit all 21 screens (or spot-check 10-12 representative ones), verify grids stack, modals go full-screen, touch targets are large enough

Accessibility test: Turn on prefers-reduced-motion in OS, visit 5 screens and verify no animations play, use Tab key to navigate through Creator Dashboard and Review Queue to verify logical order, inspect 3-4 icon buttons to verify aria-label present
Expected: Entire application feels cohesive, polished, accessible, and responsive across all devices
findings: SIDEBAR (src/v2/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx): nav icons now shift 2px right on hover via group-hover:translate-x-[2px] with a 200ms transform transition; the active indicator keeps its layoutId slide and gained a soft forest glow (shadow 0 0 8px rgba(36,76,58,.45)); count badges are motion.span keyed on the badge value so a changed count remounts and pops from scale .6 to 1 (this is the 'pulse on change' behaviour, and it re-fires only when the number actually changes); the user avatar scales to 1.05 with a brand ring plus a soft outer glow on card hover; the sign-out button scales 1.10 on hover / 0.95 on active and gained the aria-label it was missing (it previously had only title). Nav rows are h-11 (44px) on mobile and lg:h-9 on desktop, so the mobile drawer now meets the 44px touch-target guideline without loosening the desktop rail. Mobile drawer slide + backdrop blur were already correct and were left alone. GLOBAL CSS (src/index.css): added a .link-underline utility (1px underline that scales in from the left on hover/focus-visible) and applied it to the 'See all' link on the Creator Dashboard. I deliberately did NOT add badge-pulse or chevron-rotate keyframes: count pops are already handled by motion in the sidebar and disclosure chevrons already rotate from their isOpen state, so adding CSS for them would have shipped dead rules. Existing foundations were verified and kept: :focus-visible ring, button active:scale-[.985], and the global prefers-reduced-motion block that forces animation/transition duration to 0.001ms. AUDIT — EMPTY STATES: 12 of 21 views now import the shared EmptyState (AI Review, Approved Content, Exception Requests, Creator Guidelines, Sentinel Tasks, My Submissions, Notifications, Asset Library, Exceptions, Rules & Conflicts, Sentinel Monitoring, plus the Creator Dashboard recent grid). The remaining 9 (My Profile, New Content, All Submissions, Analytics & Health, Audit History, Brand Guidelines, Overview, Review Queue, Rule Impact Sandbox) still use bespoke empty markup — several are inside table cells or drawer panels where the shared card would break layout, but Overview, Review Queue and Rule Impact Sandbox could be migrated in a follow-up. AUDIT — LOADING: 6 views use the shared Skeleton components (Creator Dashboard, Brand Guidelines, Exceptions, Rule Impact Sandbox, Rules & Conflicts, Sentinel Monitoring); the other 15 use hand-rolled animate-pulse skeletons rather than a generic full-page spinner, so no screen flashes an unqualified spinner, but the skeleton markup is duplicated and should be consolidated. AUDIT — HEADINGS: every creator view renders exactly one h1. Manager views report 2-3 h1 occurrences per file, but each belongs to a mutually exclusive early return (role-denied, loading, main), so the rendered DOM always has a single h1. AUDIT — ARIA: sampled Rules & Conflicts, Exceptions, Overview and AI Review for icon-only buttons and found none unlabelled; the low aria-label counts in those files reflect that most buttons carry visible text. KNOWN GAPS LEFT OPEN (reported, not silently fixed): small icon buttons (p-1.5 / h-7) remain below the 44x44 AAA target — they meet WCAG AA, which does not set a minimum target size; 9 screens still have bespoke empty markup; skeleton markup is not centralised. Verified: npm run typecheck exits 0 with zero errors; npx vite build exits 0.
